A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, On the Coordination of Value-Maximizing Bidders. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original simulations using synthetic valuations and iPinYou-derived data, with outcomes in Table 1 and Figures 1–5, including Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains these original simulation results in Section 6, Table 1, and Figures 1–5, including Appendix D.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same independent bidding, highest-value-bidder coordination, and mirror-descent updates. V3 introduces clipped utilities and a virtual bidder for the proof only; these do not modify the bidding procedure.

E1.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D retain the same symmetric and asymmetric synthetic scenarios and simulations using the iPinYou Season 2 test data. No dataset, task, or evaluated environment is added or removed.

E2.justification: Every reported experiment retains the same comparison between Independent bidding (Algorithm 1) and Coordinated bidding (Algorithm 2), using the same mirror-descent auto-bidder.

E3.justification: The experimental settings are unchanged, including Table 1's coalition sizes and horizons, entropy mirror map, learning rate, data normalization and sampling, and utility/value metrics.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same comparisons under bidder heterogeneity and the same per-bidder learning trajectories. Appendix D retains its existing supplementary plots without adding ablations, robustness tests, or case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 independent simulations, 95% confidence intervals using 1.96 times the standard error, and the same interval-omission threshold in Table 1. Revised mathematical probability bounds belong to the theoretical analysis.

E6.justification: All eight rows of Table 1 are identical, including uncertainty values. The eight plotted panels comprising Figures 1–5 also match exactly, and the empirical findings are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 replaces v2's independent-multiplier lower-bound argument with new virtual-bidder domination, clipped-utility bounds, deterministic sublinear RoS violation, and a dual-envelope argument (v3 Lemmas B.5–B.10). The existing interior and boundary analyses are consolidated and refined. Lemma B.1 explicitly adds a strictly positive outside-bid density assumption and establishes existence of the reference multiplier.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about RoS improvement, coordinated mirror-descent value dominance, conditional optimality, and non-i.i.d. extensions. Theorem 4.2's revised optimality wording expresses the existing claim.

C2.justification: The interpretations of coalition gains and unequal individual benefits under heterogeneity remain unchanged, as do the iPinYou limitations and future-work boundaries. The substantive revisions concern proof reasoning and formal assumptions rather than a separate reinterpretation of the findings.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility disclosures are retained, including initialization, mirror map, learning rate, dataset split, normalization, and resampling procedure. No new code, hardware, or data-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 and all 32 references are unchanged. The positioning relative to utility-maximizing coordination and previous auto-bidding research is retained.

P1.justification: Section 4's proof sketch and Appendix B's exposition are substantially rewritten and reorganized. The formerly separate boundary-case subsection is integrated into a unified proof with named lemmas and revised stages. Smaller edits include an affiliation update and an introduced unresolved algorithm reference in Theorem 5.2.

P2.justification: The figures and table retain their contents and structures. Figures 1–2 shift relative to the surrounding discussion, Figure 2's caption changes slightly, and revised proof displays alter page layout. There is no substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens the central Theorem 4.1 proof: its clipped-utility and dual-envelope argument avoids v2 Claim B.2's unsupported assumption that independent bidders' utilities are bounded by B, although internal second-price payments can exceed B. The positive-density premise newly stated in Lemma B.1 remains unreconciled with the broader main-text guarantee, and a broken algorithm reference is introduced. These limitations temper, but do not outweigh, the important theoretical repair.
